phrases-21-105-psalms-quotation-righteou.title: Psalms Citation: 'The Earth — My Righteous Servants Will Inherit It'
phrases-21-105-psalms-quotation-righteou.note: Surah 21:105 explicitly cites the Psalms (al-Zabūr) by name ('We have written in the Psalms, after the Reminder: The earth – My righteous servants will inherit it'), quoting Psalm 37:29 (LXX 36:29) and its restatement in Matthew 5:5.

discussion.view: Muslim exegetes state that God here quotes the verbatim promise previously revealed to David in the Psalms (al-Zabūr) after the Torah.
discussion.reply: The clause 'The earth – My righteous servants will inherit it' matches the exact wording of Psalm 37:29 (LXX 36:29, 'the righteous shall inherit the earth') preserved in Hebrew and Greek manuscripts predating Islam by centuries.

phrases-21-105-psalms-quotation-righteou.quranEn: Certainly We have written in the Psalms, after the Reminder: ‘The earth – My righteous servants will inherit it.’
quranHighlights: We have written in the Psalms, after the Reminder: ‘The earth – My righteous servants will inherit it.’

stories-21-51-67-abraham-smashing-idols-.title: Abraham Breaking All the Idols Except the Largest One in Bereishit Rabbah
stories-21-51-67-abraham-smashing-idols-.note: Surah 21:51–67 narrates Abraham breaking his people's idols into pieces except the largest statue and telling his accusers that the largest idol did it and they should ask the statues if they can speak, matching Bereishit Rabbah 38:13.

discussion.view: Traditional commentators hold that the Quran restores the historical account of young Abraham's confrontation with his father's idolatrous community in Mesopotamia.
discussion.reply: Genesis 11:28–31 states that Terah and Abram departed from Ur of the Chaldees (`Ur Kasdim`). Because the Hebrew noun `ur` also means fire, Second Temple and rabbinic exegetes (Jubilees 12; Bereishit Rabbah 38:13) crafted a midrashic story in which Abraham breaks his father's idols, blames the largest statue, and is cast into Nimrod's furnace (`ur`).

stories-21-51-67-abraham-smashing-idols-.quranEn: [51] Certainly We gave Abraham his right (path) before (them), (for) We knew him. [52] (Remember) when he said to his father and his people: ‘What are these images which you are devoted to?’ [53] They said, ‘We found our fathers serving them.’ [54] He said, ‘Certainly you and your fathers were clearly astray.’ [55] They said, ‘Have you brought us the truth, or are you one of those who jest?’ [56] He said, ‘No! Your Lord – Lord of the heavens and the earth – is the One who created them, and I am one of the witnesses to this. [57] By God! I shall indeed plot (to destroy) your idols after you have turned away, withdrawing.’ [58] So he broke them into pieces, (all) except a big one they had, so that they would return to it. [59] They said, ‘Who has done this with our gods? Surely he is indeed one of the evildoers.’ [60] They said, ‘We heard a young man mentioning them – he is called Abraham.’ [61] They said, ‘Bring him before the eyes of the people, so that they may bear witness.’ [62] They said, ‘Have you done this with our gods, Abraham?’ [63] He said, ‘No! This big one of them did it. Just ask them, if they are able to speak.’ [64] And they turned to each other, and said, ‘Surely you – you are the evildoers.’ [65] Then they became utterly confused: ‘Certainly you know (that) these do not speak.’ [66] He said, ‘Do you serve what does not benefit you at all, or harm you, instead of God (alone)? [67] Uff to you and to what you serve instead of God! Will you not understand?’
quranHighlights: he broke them into pieces, (all) except a big one they had
He said, ‘No! This big one of them did it. Just ask them, if they are able to speak.’

sources.title: Midrash Bereishit Rabbah (Genesis Rabbah)
sources.en: One time, a certain woman came, carrying a dish of fine flour in her hand. She said to him: ‘Here, offer it before them.’ He arose, took a club in his hand, shattered all the idols, and placed the club in the hand of the largest among them. When his father came, he said to him: ‘Who did this to them?’ He said to him: ‘I will not lie to you, a certain woman came, carrying a dish of fine flour in her hand. She said to me: Here, offer it before them. I offered it before them. This one [idol] said: I shall eat first, and another one said: I shall eat first. This big idol, who was standing among them, got up and took the club and shattered them.’ He [Teraḥ] said to him: ‘What, are you mocking me? Are they sentient at all?’ He said to him: ‘Do your ears not hear what your mouth is saying?’ He [Teraḥ] took him and handed him over to Nimrod.
highlights: took a club in his hand, shattered all the idols, and placed the club in the hand of the largest among them
This big idol, who was standing among them, got up and took the club and shattered them.
Do your ears not hear what your mouth is saying?

phrases-21-104-rolling-up-heavens-like-s.title: 'We Shall Roll Up the Sky Like the Rolling Up of a Scroll for the Writings'
phrases-21-104-rolling-up-heavens-like-s.note: Surah 21:104 depicts Judgment Day as 'the Day when We shall roll up the sky like the rolling up of a scroll for the writings,' reproducing the cosmic scroll simile of Isaiah 34:4 ('the sky shall be rolled up like a scroll') and Revelation 6:14.

discussion.view: Classical commentators explain this verse as a shared prophetic depiction of the end of the cosmos revealed across scriptural dispensations.
discussion.reply: The specific simile comparing the collapsing firmament to a scribe rolling up a written scroll originates in Isaiah 34:4 and is repeated in Revelation 6:14 ('The sky was split apart like a scroll when it is rolled up'), demonstrating direct continuity with biblical apocalyptic phraseology.

phrases-21-104-rolling-up-heavens-like-s.quranEn: On the Day when We shall roll up the sky like the rolling up of a scroll for the writings: as We brought about the first creation, (so) We shall restore it – (it is) a promise (binding) on Us. Surely We shall do (it)!
quranHighlights: On the Day when We shall roll up the sky like the rolling up of a scroll for the writings

stories-21-68-70-abraham-saved-from-fier.title: God Commanding the Furnace to Be Coolness and Peace for Abraham
stories-21-68-70-abraham-saved-from-fier.note: In Surah 21:68–70, the crowd cries 'Burn him and help your gods' and God commands the fire to be 'coolness and peace for Abraham,' following the midrashic reading of 'Ur of the Chaldeans' (Genesis 11:28) as a fiery furnace in Bereishit Rabbah 38:13.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir narrate from Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid that Nimrod and his people built an enclosure of firewood, hurled Abraham into the blaze by catapult, and saw the flames rendered harmless by God's decree 'O fire, be coolness and peace.'
discussion.reply: In Genesis 11:28, 'Ur of the Chaldeans' (Hebrew Ur Kasdim, rendered in the Greek Septuagint as 'the country of the Chaldees') is the Mesopotamian city of Abraham's birth. Because the Hebrew noun ur also means 'fire' or 'flame,' Jewish exegetes in Bereishit Rabbah 38:13 read Ur Kasdim as 'the fiery furnace of the Chaldeans,' generating the narrative of Nimrod casting Abraham into the furnace echoed in 21:68–70.

stories-21-68-70-abraham-saved-from-fier.quranEn: [68] They said, ‘Burn him, and help your gods, if you are going to do (anything).’ [69] We said, ‘Fire! Be coolness and peace for Abraham!’ [70] They intended a plot against him, but We made them the worst losers,

We said, ‘Fire! Be coolness and peace for Abraham!’

sources.title: Midrash Bereishit Rabbah (Genesis Rabbah)
sources.ref: Bereishit Rabbah 38:13 (Nimrod Casting Abraham Into the Fiery Furnace and His Rescue)
sources.en: He [Teraḥ] took him and handed him over to Nimrod. He [Nimrod] said to him [Abraham]: ‘Let us bow down to fire.’ Abraham said to him: ‘Let us better bow down to water, that extinguishes fire.’ Nimrod said to him: ‘[All right,] let us bow down to water.’ He said to him: ‘If so, let us bow down to the clouds, that bear the water.’ He said to him: ‘[All right,] let us bow down to the clouds.’ He said to him: ‘If so, let us bow down to the wind, that scatters the clouds.’ He said to him: ‘[All right,] let us bow down to the wind.’ He said to him: ‘Better let us bow down to a person, who can withstand the wind.’ He said to him: ‘You are saying mere words. I bow down only to fire. I will cast you into it, and let that God to whom you bow down come and rescue you from it.’ Haran was there and he was conflicted. He said: ‘Either way [I will know what to do]; If Abraham is victorious, I will say: I am with Abraham, and if Nimrod is victorious, I will say: I am with Nimrod.’ When Abraham descended into the fiery furnace and was rescued, they said to him [Haran]: ‘With whom are you?’ He said to them: ‘I am with Abraham.’
highlights: He [Teraḥ] took him and handed him over to Nimrod. He [Nimrod] said to him [Abraham]: ‘Let us bow down to fire.’
